card.name: Inside place and era names
card.fires_on: The last piece of a proper name for a place, era or treaty, often split into parts, such as Tenmei, Landsberg, Caerleon, Charlottetown or Verdun. It appears in history and geography text.

modes.label: Place names ending
modes.description: Final piece of a split place name, often before a word like prison, School or Treaty.
modes.example: Following his trial, he was sentenced to five years in Lands<<berg>> prison, but served only six months.

modes.label: Japanese era name
modes.description: The end of the era name Tenmei just before the year number.

modes.label: Name before a following noun
modes.description: A name part before a word like Lake or Tales in a named accord or work.

card.writes: It favors Chinese tokens for temple, palace, prefecture and station, which suggests a place-name or landmark context.
card.plain: It marks the end of a historical or place name that was split into pieces, as in Landsberg or Caerleon.
